newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firms, BOJ keeps easy money stance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firms, BOJ keeps easy money stance.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen was a shade firmer on Monday amid expectations that Japan would continue its accommodative monetary policies, dealers said.
Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita told a group of business leaders Japan's monetary policies were aimed at making economic recovery firmer.
"There is nothing new from his speech. He just repeated the BOJ's accommodative rate stance," said a dealer with a European brokerage house.
Dealers said Japan finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's speech also gave little trading incentive as he reiterated what the BOJ governor had said.
At 1115 GMT, December Euroyen was at 99.05 against its IMM close of 99.04 after trading at a low of 99.03. Turnover was light, around 5,110 lots.
"December had been trapped within the range of 99.02 to 99.10 the last couple of weeks. People just bought and sold whenever these levels were reached," said a dealer with a European institution.
"These's no particular news affecting it except for Matsushita's speech," he added.
Short-term support and resistance for December Euroyen remained pegged at 99.02 and 99.08 respectively, dealers said.
The Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended lower, with June down 0.18 at 126.48 after testing a high at 126.71.
Eurodollar futures ended fairly flat. June was at 93.975 against its IMM close at 93.990 while September closed at 93.660 against 93.665 previously.
